u1-say-undecidable.title: The lint must be able to say it could not tell
u1-say-undecidable.imperative: The round-2 reviewer traced every return path. `_collects_zero` returns None when the interpreter cannot be resolved, when pytest is not importable, when there is no -k selector, or on subprocess error; `_fault_zero_collect` only appends a Fault when that value is truthy. So 'could not tell' and 'checked, found real tests' take the identical code path: no fault either way. `validate()` returns only list[Fault] with no companion channel, and main() prints either 'path: OK' or 'path: N fault(s)'. Confirmed live: the same file under two interpreters differing only in whether pytest is importable prints 'OK' for one and '1 fault(s)' for the other. An operator running under the wrong interpreter -- the single most likely way to hit this, and a host hazard CREW_CONTEXT.md documents -- gets a clean OK with no sign anything went unevaluated. This tool exists to refuse things that look fine, so a silence that looks like a pass is its worst possible failure. The rework's rule stands -- an undecidable check is not a failing check -- but the tool must be able to SAY undecidable. Add that channel: report conditions that could not be evaluated, distinctly from faults, in both the library return and the CLI output. A caller must be able to tell 'sound' from 'I could not judge N of these'. Keep the exit code semantics you have -- undecidable is not a failure -- but make it visible. Then run the full suite, rebuild map/INDEX.md, append to IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.md, and commit.
